narrative.overview: DR Web Studio sells web design and development, so the site itself is the single strongest case study in the portfolio. Every surface has one job: demonstrate the quality being sold. The system today is a competent, friendly, conversion-focused base built on Tailwind defaults: a white canvas, near-black ink, a warm orange-to-yellow gradient accent, teal as a secondary signal, Crimson Pro serif headlines over Inter body, and rounded-xl cards with a soft shadow lift on hover. It converts, and it is also close to the freelance-web-studio category default, which is what this brand is moving away from. The system steers those real tokens toward bold and modern, confident through restraint: the gradient stays but stops being the only color move; the serif carries real hierarchy; the repeated card grid, per-section eyebrow, and gradient-text hero are retired. New work should look hand-built and intentional, never templated, sterile, loud, or cluttered.
keyCharacteristics: White canvas, near-black ink; warmth carried by accent and type, not by a tinted background.
One signature accent (orange to yellow), one secondary signal (teal). Used deliberately, not everywhere.
Serif display (Crimson Pro) paired with humanist sans (Inter): contrast pairing, not two similar sans.
Flat at rest, soft lift on interaction. Depth is a response to state, not decoration.
Bilingual-safe: layouts, headlines, and labels must hold at Spanish copy lengths.

rules.name: The Earned Accent Rule
rules.body: The orange to yellow gradient is the brand's loudest move, so it is rationed: primary action plus one or two genuine moments per screen, never the default treatment for every card, icon, and heading.

rules.name: The Warmth-From-Type Rule
rules.body: Warmth comes from the accent and the serif display, never from tinting the canvas. Background stays true white (#ffffff); cream/sand/beige backgrounds are prohibited.

rules.name: The Hierarchy-By-Scale Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with size and weight contrast (>=1.25 ratio between steps), not with color or all-caps.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow-Reflex Rule
rules.body: A tiny uppercase tracked label above every section is the category tell this brand rejects. A kicker is a rare deliberate device, never the default scaffold.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards are flat at rest; shadow appears as hover/focus feedback then settles back. Never pair a 1px border with a >=16px soft drop shadow on the same element.

dos: Do keep the canvas a true white (#ffffff) and carry warmth through the accent and Crimson Pro display type.
Do ration the orange to yellow gradient: primary action plus one or two real moments per screen.
Do build hierarchy from scale and weight (>=1.25 step ratio), with text-wrap: balance on headings.
Do keep cards flat at rest and let shadow appear as hover/focus feedback only.
Do verify body text >=4.5:1 and large text >=3:1, and re-check at Spanish copy lengths (es runs longer).
Do give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
donts: Don't ship the generic SaaS/Squarespace/Wix-template look: identical icon-title-text card grids, gradient CTAs as the only color move, or a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above every section.
Don't go corporate and sterile: cold faceless agency layouts, stock photography, zero personality.
Don't go loud and flashy: over-animation, neon, gimmicky effects that distract from the work.
Don't go cluttered and busy: too much on screen, weak hierarchy, everything competing for attention.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text) on headlines; use a single solid color.
Don't use a tinted cream/sand/beige body background.
Don't round cards past 16px, or pair a 1px border with a >=16px soft drop shadow.
Don't use em dashes in copy; use commas, colons, or periods.
Don't set Crimson Pro on body or UI labels; the serif is for display only.
